chunks.text: The primary stage of wastewater treatment is the removal of both grit and primary sludge. Grit is represented in the model as solid-state silicon dioxide which is about 1% of the total inlet water flow. The grit in wastewater has a specific gravity in the range 1.5-2.7 kg/l which is much higher than that of the organic matter suspended in the influent stream (1.02 kg/l). A differential sedimentation can thus be a successful mechanism for separating grit from organic matter (Liu and Lipták, 2000) . A density-based classifier is defined as a unit operation to remove the grit in this model. The primary treatment can reduce the Total Suspended Solids (TSS) by 50-60%. Also, it implies the removal of the BOD in the incoming wastewater by 20-30%. The percentage of the sludge removal chosen in the present model is 55%.

chunks.text: Primary sedimentation is to remove the suspended solids (SS) by controlling the water flow velocity. It is required the settling time of SS shorter than the water travelling time in the tank. The SS with low density (1.1 g/mL and 1.5 g/mL) or small size but high density (1.5 g/mL) is the target pollutants to be removed in primary clarification. Most abundant MPs in the wastewater is PET followed by PE and PP (Fig. 2b ). The density of PET is between 0.96 and 1.45 g/mL. It is predicted that the primary sedimentation would catch the MPs consist of PET. However, PE and PP are difficult to be removed as they have density lower than water. Hence, wastewater containing large amount of moderate-density MPs would have high MPs removal during primary treatment.

chunks.text: The secondary clarifier is a 10-layer non-reactive system labelled from the bottom to the top. It has a total height of 4 m, and occupies a surface area of 1500 m 2 and a volume of 6000 m 3 . The tank is fed from the 6th, treated water is harvested from the 10th, and the settled sludge flows out from the first layer. A fraction of the sludge flows out of the system in the form of waste at a flow rate of 385 m 3 /d, corresponding to a biomass age of 9 days, while the other fraction is recycled externally to the first tank at a rate of 18,446 m 3 /d. The biological processes occurring in both biological reactors are simulated using the IWA Activated Sludge Model No. 1 (ASM1) proposed by [47] . This model uses thirteen state variables to track the fate of biodegradable, non-biodegradable, soluble, insoluble, nitrogen, and carbon materials. These state variables are linked to eight degradation bioprocesses occurring in biological reactors.

chunks.text: Screens and grit removal are widely employed in WWTPs as they enhance the operation and maintenance of subsequent treatment units. Recent innovations in pretreatment technologies have brought the heavy cost of grit in WWTPs operations lower which has been considered an unavoidable burden. For example, based on advanced Grit Management™, Headcell® grit separation system was developed to achieve optimum grit removal for more than 30 years in the UK and USA. Headcell® is capable of achieving 95% removal of all grit 75 μm and larger. Because of its no-moving part design involving a hydraulically driven system, it delivers grit removal over a wide range of flows in a much smaller energy footprint than the conventional removal systems (Barter and Sherony, 2011) . Table 5 lists several such advanced technologies currently being considered for pilot, demonstration, and full-scale operations in the North America.

chunks.citation: Badawi, AK et al. (2022). Advanced wastewater treatment process using algal photo-bioreactor associated with dissolved-air flotation system: A pilot-scale demonstration. J WATER PROCESS ENG.
chunks.text: Within the framework of this study, an algal photo-bioreactor combined with a dissolved air flotation system (DAF) was used for the removal of COD, BOD 5 , TSS, TN and TP from primary treated wastewater. The optimum operating conditions for the algal photo-bioreactor were determined through batch experiments, which are pH 7, temperature 25 • C, light intensity 90 μmol m − 2 S − 1 and mixing rate 100 rpm. Those optimal conditions were used in a scaled-up pilot plant treatment system to treat primary treated wastewater from ZENIN WWTP-Egypt. The operation has shown significant results where COD, BOD 5 , TSS, TN and TP have been removal with efficiencies of 56.4%, 61%, 59.2%, 48.3% and 51.7% respectively. These findings have been compared with previous studies. These findings proved the efficacy of algal-bacterial integrated treatment systems combined with DAF as a wastewater treatment technology that does not require any additional tertiary treatment to release the effluent to sewer systems.

chunks.citation: Ma, Y et al. (2009). Achieving nitrogen removal via nitrite in a pilot-scale continuous pre-denitrification plant. nan.
chunks.text:
The traditional biological nitrogen removal processes utilized in wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs) involve the oxidation of ammonium (NH 4 þ ) to nitrate (NO 3 À ) (nitrification) followed by nitrate reduction with an organic carbon source to nitrogen gas (N 2 ) (denitrification). Both nitrification and denitrification possess nitrite (NO 2 À ) as an intermediate. Hence, if

nitrification is stopped at nitrite, denitritation from nitrite to nitrogen gas can be achieved (Verstraete et al., 1977) . Nitrogen removal via nitrite yields 25% reduction in oxygen demand for nitrification and 40% reduction in chemical oxygen demand (COD) requirement for denitrification (Pollice et al., 2002; Turk and Mavinic, 1987) . The reduction in COD requirement would be particularly advantageous for WWTPs treating wastewater with a low COD to nitrogen ratio.

chunks.text: The treatment processes in the centralized WWTP consisted of pretreatment, primary treatment, biological secondary treatment (activated sludge), chlorine disinfection, and anaerobic digestion of solids. The utility operates a combined sewer system that captures both sewage and stormwater flows. In dry weather, the average concentrations of BOD 5 and TSS in the inflow wastewater of the centralized WWTP are 228 mg/L and 248 mg/L. The average dry-weather flow is 65.3 MGD (250 ML/day). In wet weather, BOD 5 and TSS concentrations are 171 mg/L and 147 mg/L. The average wet-weather flow is 119 MGD (450 ML/ day). The wastewater passes through bar screens followed by a grit removal process to remove large debris and inert solids, and then is directed to primary clarifiers for the removal of settleable solids and floatables. The primary effluent flows to the activated sludge process composed of six stages. The first two stages of the activated sludge system function as an anaerobic selector, and pure oxygen is introduced in the subsequent stages. The effluent from the aeration basins flows to 16 circular secondary clarifiers.

chunks.text: Preliminary treatment is the initial stage where coarse particles and foreign matter commonly found in raw wastewater are removed to optimize subsequent treatment processes (Sonune and Ghate, 2004) . This stage involves activities such as coarse screening, grit removal, and the comminution of large objects in wastewater. Grit chambers maintain high water velocities, preventing organic compounds from settling within the chamber. Although not all wastewater treatment plants incorporate grit removal in their preliminary treatment, some employ comminutors alongside coarse screening to reduce the size of large particles. Additionally, flow measurement devices and wave flumes are commonly used during this phase (Pachwarya et al., 2021) . It's crucial to remove oil and grease from wastewater at this stage to mitigate its adverse effects on the subsequent treatment processes. This is typically achieved through methods such as chlorination, vacuum flotation, and aeration (Pachwarya et al., 2021) .

chunks.text: The main objective of primary treatment of wastewater is the removal of settleable organic and inorganic solids by sedimentation and skimming. Here, about 50 to 60% of the total suspended solids (SS), and 65% of the oil and grease are removed along with some organic nitrogen, phosphorous, and heavy metals attached to the solids. However, the colloidal particles and dissolved constituents are not removed in this stage. Generally, gravity separation is employed in this step to separate the biosolids using either coagulation, flocculation, flotation or filtration techniques as seen in Fig. 2 . However, recent innovations in efficient wastewater treatment have brought advancements in this area (Table 4 ). For example, Salsnes filter system reported to have only 1/10th of land requirement and offers 30-60% lower investment and operating costs as compared to a conventional primary treatment system (Trojan Technologies, 2012).

chunks.text: The secondary biological treatment consists of two carrousel-shaped biological reactors with suspended biomass, equipped with two horizontal aerators, which include nitrogen removal. Regarding the sludge line, a fraction of the solids settled in the secondary settler is purged to the sludge thickener. Previously to the band filter, the sludge passes through a homogenizer to be mixed with cationic polyelectrolyte and further dewatered in the band filter prior being stored in a silo. Calafell WWTP was built on 1994 to treat the wastewaters of the municipalities of Calafell and Bellveí and designed for 70,000 population equivalent with a maximum flow of 12,000 m 3 /day. After a primary treatment, wastewater is treated in two activated sludge reactors with extended aeration including nitrogen removal, followed by the secondary settler. From these units, the treated wastewater is directly discharged to the submarine sewage. Some differences are observed in the operation of the plant between winter and summer seasons due to fluctuations on the population and changes on the influent composition. A coagulation-flocculation treatment, only operated during summer, receives the wastewater after the screening step.
